title: Trace transaction receivers and command-error semantics before moving writes
applies_when: A database or queue callback performs a state write plus an audit, replication or outbox write, and the apparent transaction boundary is a closure rather than a receiver used by every operation.
lesson: Trace the receiver of each side effect. Lexical placement inside TxPipelined does not enlist a call made through the outer Redis client: in the pinned JuiceFS incrCounter, m.rdb.IncrBy executes immediately while only genLog's pipe commands enter MULTI/EXEC. Check a failure before the transaction is sent, the counter and log together, and the returned allocated value. Do not stop at replacing the receiver. Redis continues executing later queued commands after an EXEC-time command error and does not roll back earlier writes. An unconditional queued log can therefore describe a counter increment that failed, for example on integer overflow. Test this separate error boundary, the success result, disabled logging and read-only behavior before accepting a repair. A conditional server-side operation or a checked optimistic transaction may be appropriate; justify its own failure, concurrency, retry and cluster-slot semantics rather than prescribing it from this pattern alone. When moving an allocator result through Lua, check the protocol's numeric conversion rather than assuming all signed 64-bit IDs survive it. Test positive and negative values beyond 2^53. Returning the stored decimal string avoids routing the exact ID through Lua arithmetic. Exercise an empty script cache as well as repeated concurrent allocations on a private real server.
avoid_when: This is not a universal ACID or rollback model. Determine whether the actual API implicitly enlists outer-client calls and whether the consumer requires coupled delivery. Allocator gaps can be intentional; a source mismatch alone does not prove data loss or an exploit. Transport-intercepted unit probes and Redis protocol controls are different from running a merged application, crash durability, replica promotion, full-suite correctness or performance. The maintainer accepted a simpler pipeline repair for the pre-send split; do not reopen a duplicate PR or infer that the separate command-error boundary was qualified. Establish the required supported error contract before proposing a follow-up. No prospective selection, token-cost or PR-conversion benefit follows from this owner-reviewed case.

evidence.note: Pinned incrCounter calls the outer client inside TxPipelined; genLog instead queues RPUSH and the log-version increment through pipe. Source mechanism, not an accepted fix or public execution receipt.
The changelog documents external consumption and incremental metadata sync; it is not a standalone backup. Establish a specific consumer's consistency and retry requirements before escalating impact.

Official transaction contract distinguishes failure before EXEC from errors while executing queued commands. Later commands still execute on runtime errors; Redis transactions do not support rollback.

Official Lua API documents redis.call errors, explicit key arguments and RESP-to-Lua conversions. An integer reply becomes a Lua number; a bulk string remains a string. This motivates boundary tests, not a blanket rollback, exact-integer or cluster qualification claim.

Public conditional-Lua proposal and reproducer at commit 2137311970c254a806d9f828b147b7a0f76df53e preserve the rejected unconditional-pipeline repair, exact-ID/concurrency/error controls and limits. The PR was closed, not merged, as a duplicate of author-owned PR7708 on 2026-10-20. Its earlier green CI is not merge acceptance or a reason to reopen it.

Scoped peer feedback after maintainer merge967371b: private Redis7.2.12 controls observed EXEC replies [ERR,1,1] for invalid-integer/overflow counters, leaving the counter unchanged but advancing log/version. Normal increment, discard-before-EXEC and legacy error-guard controls distinguished the boundaries. This is live Redis protocol evidence plus source inspection of head48c9b39, not execution of the merged JuiceFS package, Cluster/replay coverage or ordinary allocator failure. No competing PR was opened.
